title: Language Models Reproduce Human Reductionist Bias and Decision Inconsistency in Neurodevelopmental Disorders Assessment

bias_targets.methodology: Manipulating the placement of negative functional descriptions in fictional case vignettes of neurodevelopmental disorders to test if early exposure to negative information disproportionately influences support-allocation judgments.

Altering the emotional state (negative vs. neutral/positive) depicted in photographs attached to case descriptions to test if salient but diagnostically irrelevant visual stereotypes influence assessments of functioning.

Comparing LLM support eligibility decisions and qualitative definitions of 'basic life needs' against those of psychologists and physicians to evaluate whether models reproduce a medical reductionist framework that systematically overlooks the social and communicative needs of neurodivergent individuals.
